newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Fischler, Glickman to meet at FAO food summit.
newsitem.headline: Fischler, Glickman to meet at FAO food summit.

text.p: European Union Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler is due to meet United States Department of Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman at a World Food Summit in Rome next month, a Commission spokesman said on Friday.
"Fischler and Glickman are expected to meet during the summit," the spokesman said without giving further details.
But other sources said EU imports of genetically modified maize and soybeans from the U.S. and grain export subsidies are likely to feature high on the agenda.
The summit, which is organised by the U.N. Food and Agriculture Organisation from November 13 to 17, is intended to draw up an action plan to reduce food shortages.
In a draft report setting EU priorities for the summit, the Commission said that food security should be one of the main elements of the drive to eliminate poverty.
"The solution to the problem of food security...requires effective development strategies aimed at the reduction of inequality and elimination of poverty," it said.
This was even more important than raising food output and freeing food markets, it added.

Around 800 million people in the world, almost one person in every seven, face hunger or severe malnutrition at a time when the world is producing enough food to feed all the planet's six billion inhabitants.
Access to food will remain the key problem unless poverty, civil war and other ethnic and religious violence, and environmental damage are tackled, it said.
The EU and other industrialised countries can help by ensuring their food production policies protect the environment and by promoting food research and technological innovation.
